column3: I have but three questions for you, if you will grant me the kindness for them.
Then I shall go in peace.
SOLARIS: I'll take your silence as tacit compliance.
My first question...
When you first joined our team, were you already planning to make this happen?
Or was this simply the result of opportunism?
LIN: The only thing better than a well-laid plan coming to fruition,
Is a well-laid plan coming unraveled at the hand of impulse.
SOLARIS: I see.
Second question.
I understand your goal.
You will make the lie we promised others in order to manipulate them a reality, and create the New World.
But just what kind of world do you intend to create?
LIN: The only one where hope can exist.
LIN: The only kind worth creating.
One where anything can happen,
Whether that is everything at once, or nothing at all.
SOLARIS: Uh huh.
My third question...
LIN: I did not agree to three questions.
VICTORIA: Thanks for coming up here for me, despite how I've acted towards you.
CAL: Forgiveness was a staple of our curriculum.
I would not be who I am today without it.
VICTORIA: Y-yeah...
You really saved Kiki's Medicham, huh?
CAL: Yeah.
Do you want to meet her again?
VICTORIA: Not right now.
Let's... do it back at Apophyll.
You'll come with me, right?
I could use some help, between that place and Reborn City duties.
CAL: After this is all over...
Yeah, I can do that.
But there's something I still need to do first.
VICTORIA: Oh...
That's okay.
Whenever you get back, then.
It's been a long time, hasn't it...
CAL: I guess so.
VICTORIA: Um...
This--
Might be a little weird for me to say given how long I've been mad at you, but...
Um, back then I...
I really liked you.
Do you think...
Maybe once things settle down...
We could... go out, or something?
CAL: Oh.
Uh...
This is... a little awkward.
I'm, uh...
Not... actually...
...Into women?
VICTORIA: ...Oh!
Oh.
Oh-- okay.
Okay, well!
It's a long trip back to Apophyll from here, so I guess I'll get started!
I, uh, hope to see you around someday!
Bye!
I'll get in touch with her later.
For now...
I'll go back and look for him, I guess.

RADOMUS: Well, well, well.
This is quite a mess, isn't it?
That lad dropped me off here and went to search for the way forward, and here we are.
I feel that I can safely assume you've had some experience with these contraptions by now, and I believe I've a solid enough understanding of it.
Shall we get right to it?
But I will say... looking at this data...
Whoever designed this surely had either a veritable sadistic streak, or a very good sense of humor.
I suspect we shall never find out which.
RADOMUS: What will your move be?
RADOMUS: Very well. This will be a mite complicated...
RADOMUS: If there were an award for the most inefficient data system in all of history, they surely would have won it.
RADOMUS: Shall we try? Very well.
RADOMUS: Hm.
And there it is.
Impressive as always.
I will fetch Hardy from wherever he's gotten to exploring, and we'll go on ahead.
RADOMUS: It would seem that wasn't quite it.
Permit me just a moment to try something on my end...
RADOMUS: There it is.
There is no use in holding ourselves against systems this arbitrary.
Ah, but I believe I'm putting the pieces together myself.
Take another try, and give me just another moment more to perfect an approach.
This will continue to be rather challenging until you can properly draw the necessary inferences.
Let's take this clue as an example:
5. The Hardness of the "Small" gem is less than the Hardness of the Amethyst, which is less than the Hardness of the "Pure" Gem.
It may not appear to give us any concrete information at first, but that's far from the case.
If the "Small" gem is softer than Amethyst, then we know that Amethyst is not "Small".
Conversely, we also hereby know that Amethyst is not "Pure", and further that the "Small" gem is not "Pure".
This allows us to rule out several possibilities-- and of course, it is only one clue.
With eight such similar ones, I have faith that inferring these eliminated possibilities will reveal only one possible outcome.
But that may be difficult to imagine without marking it down visually somehow.
Surely you have not come this far without being able to do so?
This system is rather unfortunate, isn't it?
RADOMUS: Instructions?
It's nearly a miracle that the constructor of this convoluted contraption considered to create such things.
Simply read the available dataset as if they were 'clues' to a puzzle.
Using your powers of logic, deduction, and perhaps drawing a lot of boxes on paper, figure out all the qualities each of four crystals has.
We then input those qualities as data back into the system by moving the colored blocks to our right in line with the screens displaying those qualities.
For example, a Ruby with a "Coxcomb" Habit requires the red block to be moved in front of the screen that reads "Coxcomb".
It is tedious and nonsensical, but then, aren't all things?
Complete.
You there!
Pick your head up and hold it high!
When everything seems lost and you're at the end of the road, I want you to remind yourself, to never give up, and never stop fighting.

FERN: I know what I said before, but I didn't think YOU, of all people, would actually make it this far.
Gotta be honest, it's genuinely impressive,
Just how consistently you've cheated and lucked your way forward.
FERN: You remember what I said back at the school?
Someone like you doesn't deserve to move forward here.
What've you done, huh?
Forget accomplishments-- why do YOU deserve it more than anyone else?!
Can you really answer that?
Can you look me in the eyes and tell me why,
No matter how hard anyone tries,
YOU get to be the one to step on them?
If it's gotta be someone, it should be me.
What right do you have? you might ask.
To which I say,
Fuck off.
FLORINIA: Fern.
FERN: You stay out of this, Flobot!
This is between me and \PN,
And no one else.
I'll beat you here and take the rest of your badges for myself!
FERN: It should've been me...
It should've been--
It should still be...
But YOU got in the way!
FERN: WHAT?!
What do you want, you stupid doll?
FLORINIA: I am not a doll.
Nor am I a robot.
I have feelings, and I've run from them.
And it will take a lot more experimentation and research until I am able to fully receive or understand them.
But like fermions, bosons and everything else, one can be sure they are there.
FERN: Believe me, I care deeply.
FLORINIA: This speaker is not a doll.
FERN: You sure resemble one.
FLORINIA: Your behavior is irrational.
It is suggested to withdraw from the present conflict at once.
FERN: That's what I thought.
Everyone's just against me.
You always have been.
FLORINIA: Incorrect.
FERN: Where's your fucking evidence, huh?
You never cared back then, and even now you're still here trying to stop me!
And you just snatched the place right up!
You wanna know why I should be the one to finish the league?
Because then, maybe--
Just fucking maybe--
If I were the champion,
Maybe someone would actually smile at me.
Yeah?
Cuz no one ever bothered to.
Our parents sure didn't.
Anything I did well, she got the credit for.
And anything she did wrong, I got the blame for.
Flobot would never smile.
She actually used to, you know that?
You believe it?
But not at me.
Never at me.
The other students--
I wasn't always top of the pack.
More like the rock bottom of it.
But I fixed that.
I learned to persevere,
To TAKE control.
But when you're at the top, then they don't smile for a different reason.
They're too afraid.
Everyone's a fucking coward.
What does it cost, huh?
To make another person feel like they aren't just the scum of the earth?
That's why even now, I try to face a challenge with a smile!
And if I can't--
Then I just have to make something worth smiling about!
Lin could do that.
Better than anyone else can.
God knows there's too little in this world that's worth it,
Or none of us would even be here right now.
LIN: That is correct.
LIN: In this world, all things operate within scarcity.
Resources are finite.
Space and time are finite.
Compassion is finite.
This is the world once birthed by Arceus of its own will.
This is not a world that must be accepted.
With a wisdom that both humans and Arceus lacked so long ago, we can guide creation to a world where these limits need not apply.
FERN: Gotta say, I've never been so glad to see you.
FERN: Anyway, even you should get it now.
I'm only here because of you, \PN.
You got in the way of me just staying peacefully at school.

They steal all the glory in everything they do.
Whether it's luck or some other kind of bullshit, they always just happened to be at the right place at the right time.

Spinel Town?

When I had the opportunity, I decided to go with the ones who actually gave me a chance.

FERN: \PN would only accept me being around them to use me for free healing between battles.
That's the case for everyone, right?
There's no gratitude there, and it doesn't matter what they think of the other person as long as they're of use.
FLORINIA: Utility is not the only benefit of cooperation.
Individuals participating in mutually beneficial activities for the sake of the same goal often observe increased friendliness between them.
LIN: Victory shared is victory halved.
FERN: Please.
\PN only cares about what others do for them.
